title: City Reliquary

card.teaser: An identity for a museum of everyday objects, built on a negative-space CR mark.

summary: A visual identity for City Reliquary, a community-focused New York City museum, built around a collage-like CR mark formed from overlapping rectangular frames.
meta: CR mark, identity system, posters, signage

hero.alt: A red t-shirt printed with the white City Reliquary mark, worn against a graffitied wall.

text: City Reliquary celebrates New York City's history through everyday objects, personal collections, and overlooked artifacts. The identity draws on the idea of collecting and preserving fragments of history, using a collage of frames to create a distinctive mark that reflects the museum's approach.

blocks.label: Research
blocks.heading: Objects worth keeping.
blocks.body: City Reliquary collects everyday artifacts and the stories attached to them. I started by looking at the objects, signs and handmade ephemera the museum is built around.

blocks.caption: Research.

blocks.label: Sketches
blocks.heading: Finding the mark.
blocks.body: I sketched the C and R together until they shared one shape, with the negative space doing the work of the second letter.
blocks.alt: Sketches of the City Reliquary CR mark.
blocks.caption: Mark sketches.

finalDesign: The logo is constructed from a collage of outlined rectangular frames arranged in a compact, overlapping composition. The frames create a sense of layered images and collected fragments, while the negative space between them forms the initials C and R. This allows the mark to function as both a monogram and a visual reference to the museum's collection of objects and stories.

The identity uses a limited palette of rust red and white. The mark appears alongside a condensed *City Reliquary Museum* wordmark on a tote bag, while a larger, cropped version covers a red spiral notebook. The same elements carry across a mug, cap, and pens, adapting to different surfaces and scales.

The overlapping frames give the identity its structure and visual character. Keeping the palette and core mark consistent allows the applications to feel connected, while changes in scale and cropping introduce variation without losing recognition.
